messages:
alex: Heads-up — after rolling runtime v2.14 to canary yesterday (~02:10 UTC) we started seeing a p99 jump on /v1/generate for a small tenant cohort. Baseline p99 ~220ms -> spike ~900ms. No obvious error rate increase.

maria: Noted. Is this only in canary or also hitting prod traffic?

alex: Only canary pool so far (canary-tag=fast-path). Dataset: ~5k reqs/min. Spike started ~02:25 and persisted.

tim: Throwing first checks at infra: are kernels pinned? any cold starts?

alex: Kernel selector changed in v2.14 (attempt to pick vectorized kernels for short sequences). Logs show a subset of requests landed on the new selector path. No container restarts.

jess: Can you paste the PromQL for p99 you're watching?

alex: Sure —
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",env="canary"}[5m])) by (le))
```
Also saw per-instance tail high on a few hosts: host-23, host-29.

sre-bot: @channel Incident created: INC-2026-815 - canary p99 spike (link: https://incidents/redwood/INC-2026-815) :rotating_light:

maria: Can we repro locally with the canary image + same model? If it's kernel selection, a small repro might surface it.

tim: I ran a small synthetic against the canary image with short seqs (<=64 tokens) and saw elevated tail when batch sizes hit 8-12. Might be a batching edge with the new kernel.

alex: Good catch — the affected requests had heterogeneous prompt sizes (mix of 16 and 512 tokens) — maybe scheduler isn't isolating short-paths, and kernel selection ends up using a slower fallback for big sequences causing head-of-line delay.

jess: Steps to mitigate now? Options: roll back canary, route tenant off canary, or disable new selector flag. Which is fastest?

maria: Short-term: route affected tenant cohort to stable runtime and set canary cutoff to 0 for that routing policy. Medium: revert selector or ship a quick scheduler fix.

alex: I pushed a routing tweak to divert the cohort at the policy layer to stable. Policy change applied (ID: route-pol-778). Observing metrics...

sre-bot: Action taken: traffic-split update applied to tenant acme-corp -> 100% stable (audit: route-pol-778).

tim: While traffic flips, let's capture a heap of traces for the old vs new path to confirm where time is spent. Query:
```
trace_search("service:runtime AND route:/v1/generate AND env:canary", limit:100)
```
Also collect kv-cache hit rates per host.

alex: Collected traces — new-path shows blocking on `kernel_prepare()` for ~300-400ms on tail calls on hosts 23/29. Old path shows <50ms.

jess: That suggests kernel selection is doing some per-request compile or memory pinning. Any increased iowait on those hosts?

maria: Node metrics show occasional iowait bumps coinciding with the kernel_prepare spikes. Looks like a memory-copy path triggered for the vectorized kernel under certain seq-length patterns.

tim: For a fast mitigation I recommend two actions: 1) disable vectorized-kernel selector flag in canary (remote config) to avoid the slow path, 2) keep cohort routed to stable until we validate.

alex: I flipped remote-config key `runtime.vectorized_selector_enabled=false` for canary. Patch applied at 03:02 UTC.

sre-bot: Remote config change detected: runtime.vectorized_selector_enabled set to false on canary (by alex).

jess: After disabling, p99 dropped back toward baseline within 2 minutes. Can you post the before/after p99 numbers?

alex: Before: avg p99 (02:30–02:40) = 912ms. After disable: avg p99 (03:05–03:15) = 240ms. Still slightly above stable but much better.

maria: Good. Next steps: 1) add a safety guard in kernel selector to avoid choosing vectorized path when seq-length variance in batch > threshold, 2) add a canary test that simulates heterogeneous prompt sizes, 3) instrument kernel_prepare latency with a histogram tag for path type.

tim: I'll own the selector guard and the histogram. Target: PR today, canary patch tomorrow.

jess: I'll open a postmortem-lite in INC-2026-815 with timeline and mitigations. Also notify Support to follow up with affected customers explaining we routed them to stable and are working on a fix.

support-notify: Notifying account team + CS: "We've routed your traffic to stable runtime while we investigate a perf regression in our canary build. No request loss. Follow-up incoming."

alex: Notes for triage doc: include repro harness (mix seq lengths 16/512, batch 8-12), PromQL, trace filter, hosts-of-interest, and the remote-config toggle to flip in emergencies.

maria: Also add a small automated canary check: generate a mixed-length workload and assert p99 < 350ms for short-path cohort. Add to canary pipeline.

tim: Will add tests and a perf regression alert rule that triggers on canary p99 deltas > 2x stable for 5m.

jess: Closing loop: rollback avoided, quick remote-config toggle + routing change mitigated customer impact. Assigning action items in the incident doc. Great collaboration. :tada:
